id: ISS-0950
title: "Catalog service endpoint_url is not URL-validated at registration/publish time (decision 0027 gap)"
discovered_by: SECURITY-REVIEWER
discovered_in_run: WF03-ISS0917-20261001 (filed by ORCH)
discovered_at: "2026-10-01T14:06:29Z"
severity: MINOR
owner: "ELIXIR-DEV"
description: >
  Found by SECURITY-REVIEWER in WF03-ISS0917-20261001. POST /service-catalog and publish do no
  UrlValidator check on endpoint_url; the only control is the dispatch-time INV-9 gate in
  ServiceTaskDispatcher.http_transport/3. ISS-0917's fix makes catalog endpoints reachable by the
  dispatcher for the first time, so add fast-feedback syntactic validation (https scheme, host not
  private/loopback literal) at register/publish time in Letflow.ServiceCatalog /
  Routers.AdminServices. Defense in depth; dispatch gate stays binding. Severity MINOR (hardening).
  Owner ELIXIR-DEV (via CODE-DESIGNER).
affected_files:
  - lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex
  - lib/letflow/routers/admin_services.ex
queue_ref: Q-921  # queue issue_ref ISS-0921 collides with an existing local file; local filename ISS-0950
github_ref: GH-2095
status: open

task.description: WF-03 Step 0.5 (registry lookup: docs/issues/*.yaml resolved entries about catalog endpoint_url / UrlValidator / INV-9 / service catalog registration) + Step 1 (diagnose), combined. Work in the main checkout C:/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow-3 on branch feature/WF03-ISS0950-20261001 (already created and pushed; do not switch branches; do not touch main or other sessions' branches). IMPORTANT: this issue's local file is docs/issues/ISS-0950.yaml (queue ref Q-921, GH #2095); docs/issues/ISS-0921.yaml is a DIFFERENT issue, ignore it. Reproduce against the real code (scratch test or iex-free mix run; MIX_ENV=test; Postgres is up; machine is shared so run only scoped tests, never the full suite): show that POST /service-catalog (and the publish path) accepts endpoint_url values like http://127.0.0.1/x, http://169.254.169.254/, https://10.0.0.5/, ftp://x, and non-URLs, and that only ServiceTaskDispatcher.http_transport/3 rejects them at dispatch (INV-9). Report with file:line evidence: (1) where endpoint_url enters (Letflow.ServiceCatalog register/publish/update/new-version functions, Routers.AdminServices handlers, any changeset), all write paths that can set endpoint_url (including solution-pack install per decision 0027 docs/migration/decisions/0027-solution-pack-service-catalog-install-policy.md); (2) the existing Letflow UrlValidator (name/location/API, what it checks, whether it does DNS or syntactic only, how the dispatcher gate calls it) so the fix can reuse it, not reinvent it; (3) how register/publish errors are shaped and mapped to HTTP (existing error tuples/status codes, tests asserting them) so a new validation error fits the convention; (4) what decision 0027 says about install-time vs register-time endpoint validation and whether any rule constrains the fix; (5) existing tests that would be affected (e.g. fixtures using http:// or example.test hosts in service-catalog tests) -- list them, because a stricter validator may break fixtures; (6) interplay with ISS-0917 (just merged, 2bc51bdd). Do NOT implement the fix. Complete the handoff with next_action Route to CODE-DESIGNER.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause stated with file:line evidence and real reproduction output quoted
Reusable UrlValidator API and dispatcher gate call identified
No lib/ test/ web/ changes left behind (git status --porcelain lib/ test/ web/ empty)

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 REGISTRY LOOKUP: grepped docs/issues/*.yaml for endpoint_url / UrlValidator / INV-9 / service catalog. No resolved entry covers register/publish-time endpoint_url validation (ISS-0917 fixed dispatch resolution only; ISS-0922/0923 are different catalog gaps; ISS-0950 itself is the only match). Not a recurrence. The gap is already named, in prose, as a deliberately deferred residual risk in decision 0027 (SECURITY-REVIEWER sign-off, INV-9 point 3).

ROOT CAUSE (reproduced, MIX_ENV=test, scratch script outside the repo, DB rows cleaned up afterwards: 'deleted 11 entries, 5 versions'): nothing on any catalog write path validates endpoint_url beyond presence and length. Letflow.ServiceCatalog.Entry.insert_changeset/2 (lib/letflow/service_catalog/entry.ex:142-158) does validate_required + validate_length(:endpoint_url, max: 2048) (line 147); Entry.publish_changeset/2 (entry.ex:183-215) the same (line 209). ServiceCatalog.register/1 (service_catalog.ex:214-243) and publish/3 -> do_publish -> apply_publish (service_catalog.ex:337-408) call no UrlValidator. The router handlers AdminServices.handle_register (admin_services.ex:212-242) and handle_publish (admin_services.ex:292-324) pass the raw body string through. The only URL control is the dispatch-time gate ServiceTaskDispatcher.http_transport/3,4 (service_task_dispatcher.ex:304-338; 3-arity at 306 honours test flag :service_task_ssrf_validation_enabled; 4-arity at 331 calls UrlValidator.validate(rendered_url, dns_resolver) and returns {:request_build_error, :target_url_not_allowed}).

REPRODUCTION OUTPUT (real, trimmed): POST /admin/services as PLATFORM_ADMIN via Routers.AdminServices.call/2 returned 201 for endpoint_url = 'http://127.0.0.1/x', 'http://169.254.169.254/', 'https://10.0.0.5/', 'https://127.0.0.1/', 'ftp://x', 'not a url', '{{variables.absent}}', 'https://example.test/iss0917/{{variables.region}}/svc', 'https://[::1]/x'; only '' got 422 (validate_required). The same URLs through UrlValidator.validate/2 (stub resolver) and ServiceTaskDispatcher.http_transport/4 all returned {:error, :target_url_not_allowed} / {:request_build_error, :target_url_not_allowed}, so the dispatch gate is the sole control. ServiceCatalog.publish/3 returned :ok and stored 'http://127.0.0.1/x', 'http://169.254.169.254/', 'https://10.0.0.5/', 'ftp://x', 'not a url' (each archiving the previous version). ServiceCatalog.register/1 called directly accepted 'http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data'. (The issue text says 'POST /service-catalog'; the real mount is /admin/services, lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex:178; /services at :177 is read-only. Decision 0027 repeats the wrong path.)

(1) ENDPOINT_URL WRITE PATHS (grep of ServiceCatalog.register|publish in lib/ outside design docs): (a) ServiceCatalog.register/1, called only from AdminServices.handle_register (admin_services.ex:225, POST /admin/services, :AdminServicesManage); (b) ServiceCatalog.publish/3, called only from AdminServices.handle_publish (admin_services.ex:304, POST /admin/services/:service_id/versions). publish also copies the PREVIOUS endpoint_url into service_catalog_versions via archive_current_version (service_catalog.ex:361-381; existing data, not new input). update_scope/2 casts only scope/owner_tenant_id (entry.ex:164-174); retire/1 casts nothing. Solution-pack install is NOT a write path: SolutionPack.check_unsupported_sections/1 (solution_pack.ex:1305-1306) hard-rejects any non-empty service_catalog_entries with {:error, :unsupported_pack_section}; priv/modules/exam/pack.json:743 has service_catalog_entries: []. So there are exactly two input points, both in one router. Put the check at the context/changeset layer so both are covered (INV-RT-1 forbids Repo calls in routers; a pure validation call is fine anywhere).

(2) UrlValidator: Letflow.Webhooks.UrlValidator, lib/letflow/webhooks/url_validator.ex. API: validate/1 (line 39, real DNS via default_resolver/1) and validate/2 (line 43, injectable dns_resolver). Returns :ok | {:error, :target_url_not_allowed}. Checks: scheme must be exactly 'https' (check_scheme, line 97); host non-nil/non-empty (101-102); IP-literal hosts against blocklist 127/8, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 169.254/16, ::1, fc00::/7, fe80::/10, IPv4-mapped/compatible v6 (blocked_ipv4?/blocked_ipv6?, 150-174); hostnames are RESOLVED via dns_resolver and every address checked; DNS failure = blocked (resolve_and_check, 134-148). So it is NOT syntactic-only: any non-IP host does DNS, and there is no public syntactic-only entry point. Other callers: Webhooks.create/2 (webhooks.ex:154, validate/1 with real DNS) and Webhooks dispatch_http (webhooks.ex:385). Reuse options for CODE-DESIGNER: (i) call validate/2 with an always-public stub resolver, e.g. fn _ -> {:ok, [{:inet, {203,0,113,1}, []}]} end (checks scheme, host, IP literals; never touches DNS); (ii) add a small public validate_syntactic/1 to UrlValidator. Either way do not copy the blocklist. Not covered by the validator at all (pre-existing, out of scope): 0.0.0.0, 100.64.0.0/10, multicast.

CRITICAL DESIGN CONSTRAINT 1, endpoint_url is a TEMPLATE: Engine.resolve_service_task_arm_attrs renders resolved.endpoint_url through the {{variables.KEY}} renderer (engine.ex:980-984, comment 962-964), and tests deliberately register 'https://example.test/iss0917/{{variables.region}}/svc' and '{{variables.absent}}' (test/letflow/engine_catalog_service_task_test.exs:346, 363). A register-time check on the raw string must therefore define how placeholders are treated: a placeholder in the path is harmless, a placeholder in scheme/host position cannot be validated (and is itself an SSRF smell). CODE-DESIGNER must decide the policy, and what to do with the fixture '{{variables.absent}}' (it asserts the engine's url_rendered_empty error at activation).

CRITICAL DESIGN CONSTRAINT 2, no DNS at register time: every test fixture uses https://example.test/... (.test is reserved, NXDOMAIN); real-DNS validate/1 at register time would reject all of them (default_resolver returns {:error, :nxdomain} -> blocked). DNS at admin time also adds latency/flakiness and the dispatch gate re-does it anyway (rebinding). So the register/publish check must be syntactic/literal-IP only; the dispatch gate stays binding.

(3) ERROR SHAPING / HTTP MAPPING: register/1 spec returns {:ok, Entry} | {:error, Ecto.Changeset} | {:error, :tenant_not_found} | {:error, :duplicate_service_id} (service_catalog.ex:209-213); publish/3 returns {:ok,_} | {:error,:not_found} | {:error,:duplicate_version} | {:error, Changeset} (327-331). Router maps (admin_services.ex:225-237 and 304-316): :tenant_not_found -> Response.unprocessable 'owner_tenant_id does not name an existing tenant' (422); :duplicate_service_id -> Response.conflict (409); :duplicate_version -> conflict; ANY Ecto.Changeset -> Response.unprocessable(conn, 'validation failed') (422, generic detail, no field leakage). Lowest-friction fit: add the check as a changeset validation (validate_change on :endpoint_url in insert_changeset near line 147 and publish_changeset near line 209) so it surfaces as {:error, %Changeset{}} and the routers need NO change, yielding 422 'validation failed' like every other field error. An alternative typed atom {:error, :endpoint_url_not_allowed} would need new clauses in both router case statements (a missing clause = CaseClauseError/500) plus @spec updates. Precedent warning: Webhooks.create/2 returns {:error, :target_url_not_allowed} (webhooks.ex:147,154) but Routers.Webhooks.handle_create (routers/webhooks.ex:159-166) has only a Changeset clause; by code reading that atom would raise CaseClauseError. I did NOT run it, flag only. Tests: grep of test/letflow/routers/admin_services* and service_catalog* shows no existing test asserting a 422 'validation failed', so new tests are additive.

(4) DECISION 0027: packed service_catalog_entries are permanently NOT permitted (Decision section 1); catalog entries are provisioned only via the out-of-band admin route (Consequences, line 443). So 0027 imposes NO install-time endpoint validation requirement (there is no install path). Its SECURITY-REVIEWER sign-off, INV-9 point 3 (lines 515-535), names this exact gap as pre-existing and 'currently inert' because the dispatcher catalog lookup was a stub, and says that once the stub is replaced (ISS-0917, now merged as 2bc51bdd) the missing registration-time or dispatch-time check 'becomes a live INV-9 question'. The dispatch-time check already exists on the catalog path (see 6), so what remains is registration-time hardening only. No rule in 0027 constrains the fix beyond: do not add any pack-install code (solution_pack.ex stays untouched). Note 0027's wrong path 'POST /service-catalog' (actual POST /admin/services). INV-9 in docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md requires validation at the request call site, not ingestion alone, hence defense in depth only; do not remove or weaken the dispatch gate.

(5) FIXTURES AT RISK (all use https://example.test/...; none uses http:// or a private IP, so all survive a syntactic https+host+IP-literal check except the one flagged): test/letflow/service_catalog_test.exs:102 (base fixture), 910, 947, 954, 1002 (its raw-SQL INSERTs at 184-250 and 855/890 bypass the changeset and are unaffected); test/letflow/routers/admin_services_test.exs:107; test/letflow/routers/admin_services_publish_retire_test.exs:98,123,147,175,190; test/letflow/service_catalog_resolve_pinned_version_test.exs:60,77,102,158; test/letflow/engine_pin_resolver_catalog_test.exs:74,221,313; test/letflow/engine_catalog_service_task_test.exs:44-45 (@v1_url/@v2_url), 71, 89, 346 (template in PATH only, survives); test/letflow/routers/tasks_test.exs:2216-2294 (register_catalog_entry!); test/support/service_catalog_reaper_test.exs:74. WILL FAIL a strict check: test/letflow/engine_catalog_service_task_test.exs:363, register_with!(%{endpoint_url: '{{variables.absent}}'}), which is not a URL (needs redesign or template-tolerant policy). Outside ExUnit: web/tests/e2e/pipelines/platform-instance-pin-survives-catalog-change.pipeline.e2e.spec.ts:120-124 builds endpoint URLs from SERVICE_TASK_MOCK_BASE_URL (default https://httpbin.org/anything, fine; breaks if CI sets an http:// or localhost mock base); web/src/pages/admin/services/ServicesPage.tsx sends endpoint_url from a free-text form (a new 422 shows the existing generic failure). Tests that set :service_task_ssrf_validation_enabled=false (service_task_wiring_test, service_task_dispatcher_test, req208_meridian_test) use inline url_template, not catalog registration, so are unaffected.

(6) INTERPLAY WITH ISS-0917 (2bc51bdd): that fix made catalog endpoints reachable by the dispatcher (Engine renders the PINNED version's endpoint_url at activation, freezes it in config_snapshot, dispatcher calls http_transport/3 -> UrlValidator gate). The dispatch gate therefore still applies to the catalog path, and my reproduction shows it rejects every bad URL, so exposure is bounded: no outbound request to a private address can result. The real impact of ISS-0950 is (a) late failure: a bad URL is accepted at admin time and only fails as a non-retriable request_build_error when an instance runs, after pinning; (b) published bad versions are archived and stay resolvable (resolve_pinned_version applies no endpoint check). Recommend already-stored bad rows are tolerated (dispatch gate covers them; no migration/backfill). No conflict with ISS-0922/0923. The fix must not touch resolve_pinned_version/3 or the engine.

SEVERITY: MINOR stands (defense in depth, dispatch gate binding, only PLATFORM_ADMIN can write).

SCOPE FOR CODE-DESIGNER (not implemented here): add a pure endpoint_url format check to Entry.insert_changeset/2 and Entry.publish_changeset/2 reusing UrlValidator (no DNS, template-aware), surfaced as a changeset error (422 'validation failed'), no router change needed. Tests: bad-URL table for register and publish (http://, ftp://, non-URL, 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, 10.0.0.5, [::1]) -> {:error, %Changeset{}} and 422 via the router, plus a template-bearing happy path; resolve the '{{variables.absent}}' fixture; no change to the dispatcher gate. Working tree check: git status --porcelain lib/ test/ web/ is empty; only this handoff file is modified (scratch script lives in the session scratchpad, outside the repo).

issues.description: Handoff, ISS-0950 and decision 0027 name the route 'POST /service-catalog'; the real mount is POST /admin/services (lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex:178). Docs drift, not blocking.

Routers.Webhooks.handle_create (lib/letflow/routers/webhooks.ex:159-166) has no clause for {:error, :target_url_not_allowed} that Webhooks.create/2 can return (webhooks.ex:147,154). Found by code reading only, NOT reproduced by running; possible latent CaseClauseError/500. Candidate for a separate issue, not part of ISS-0950.

Design hazard: endpoint_url is a {{variables.KEY}} template rendered at activation (engine.ex:980-984); fixture test/letflow/engine_catalog_service_task_test.exs:363 registers the non-URL '{{variables.absent}}' and would fail a strict register-time check. CODE-DESIGNER must specify template handling.

UrlValidator has no syntactic-only entry point; validate/1 does real DNS, which would reject every https://example.test fixture (NXDOMAIN). Fix must use validate/2 with a stub resolver or add a public no-DNS function.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER (design the register/publish-time endpoint_url check per the SCOPE FOR CODE-DESIGNER paragraph; owner ELIXIR-DEV; REVIEWER and SECURITY-REVIEWER gates apply, INV-9)
